title: A2.7 sample flipped: expand then complete the square on 3(x − 1)^2 + 4
stem_student: Given the vertex form f(x) = 3(x − 1)^2 + 4, express the equation in standard form. Use technology to compare the graphs of these two forms of the equation. Then start from the standard-form writing you produced and complete the square to recover vertex form. Confirm both rewrites leave the graph unchanged.
stem_teacher: First two sentences are the verbatim A2.7 seed sample (lms/seeds/mcf3m_expectations.json). The CTS flip is LLOVES-owned review on that same Ministry function — A2.7 REVIEW only; do not new-teach expansion. Companion L1 item mcf3m-m4-ontario-a27-sample is expand-only.
answer: Standard form 3x^2 − 6x + 7. Completing the square recovers 3(x − 1)^2 + 4. The graphs coincide.
answer_verification: Seed has no key for the A2.7 sample. Author-computed expand: 3(x − 1)^2 + 4 = 3(x^2 − 2x + 1) + 4 = 3x^2 − 6x + 7. Author-computed CTS: 3(x^2 − 2x) + 7 = 3(x^2 − 2x + 1) + 7 − 3 = 3(x − 1)^2 + 4.
